zh: 問曰：用心坐中治病，必有効不？答曰：若具十法，無有不益。十法者：一、信；二、用；三、勤；四、恒住緣中；五、別病因起；六者、方便；七、久行；八、知取捨；九、善將護；十、識遮障。何謂為信？謂信此法必能治病。何謂為用？謂隨時常用。何謂為勤？用之專精不息，取得汗為度。何謂為恒住緣中？謂細心念念，依法而不散亂。何謂別病因起？別病因起如上說。何謂為方便？謂吐納運心緣想，善巧成就，不失其宜。何謂為久行？謂若用之未即有益，不計日月，常習不廢。何謂知取捨？謂知益則勤，用損則捨之，漸轉心取治。何謂知將護？謂善識異緣犯觸。何謂遮障？謂得益不向外說，未損不疑謗。若依此十法所治，必定有効。
en: Question: is applying the mind while sitting to treat illness certain to be effective? Answer: if the ten conditions are all present, there is no case where it fails to benefit. The ten conditions are: faith; application; diligence; constantly dwelling within the object; distinguishing the illness's cause; skillful means; sustained practice over time; knowing what to take up and what to set aside; skillfully guarding and protecting oneself; and recognizing obstruction.

What is meant by faith? Believing that this method is truly able to treat the illness. What is meant by application? Applying it constantly, at every appropriate time. What is meant by diligence? Applying it with single-minded devotion, without pause, taking the breaking of a sweat as the measure. What is meant by constantly dwelling within the object? A fine, attentive mind, moment to moment, relying on the method without becoming scattered. What is meant by distinguishing the illness's cause? Distinguishing its cause exactly as described above. What is meant by skillful means? Skillfully and successfully coordinating the breath, the movement of the mind, and visualization together, without losing what is proper to the moment. What is meant by sustained practice over time? Even if the method brings no immediate benefit, continuing to practice it without ever abandoning it, regardless of how many days or months pass. What is meant by knowing what to take up and what to set aside? Knowing that where it benefits, one should apply it diligently, and where it causes harm, one should set it aside, gradually redirecting the mind toward what actually treats the condition. What is meant by skillfully guarding and protecting oneself? Properly recognizing other conditions that may intrude upon and disturb the treatment. What is meant by recognizing obstruction? Not speaking of one's benefit to others, and not doubting or denouncing the method before any harm has actually occurred. If one relies on these ten conditions in treatment, there is certain to be an effect.

The ten conditions read less like a meditation instruction and more like a general theory of what makes any sustained self-treatment actually work — faith and diligence at the start, accurate diagnosis and skillful coordination in the middle, and, at the end, two conditions about patience with slow results and quiet discretion about outcomes either way. The closing pair — not boasting when it works, not doubting or denouncing it before any harm has occurred — targets a specific failure mode: undermining a treatment through impatience or through talking about it prematurely, before it has had the chance to actually work. This closes the fourth of the internal expedient means' five layers.

zh: 次第五、明魔事者，魔羅，秦言殺者。奪行人功德之財，殺智慧命，故名魔羅。云何名魔事？如佛以功德智慧度脫眾生，入涅槃為事。魔亦如是，常以破壞眾生善根，令流轉生死為事。若能安心道門，道高則魔盛，故須善識魔事。今釋即為三：一、分別魔法不同；二、明魔事發相；三、明壞魔之法。
en: Next, the fifth layer of the internal expedient means, clarifying demonic affairs: Māra, in the Qin-dynasty translation, means "the killer." It seizes the wealth of the practitioner's merit and kills the very life of wisdom — hence it is named Māra. What is meant by "demonic affairs"? Just as the Buddha takes liberating sentient beings through merit and wisdom, entering nirvāṇa, as his own work, Māra is exactly the same: it constantly takes destroying sentient beings' wholesome roots and keeping them turning through birth-and-death as its own work. If one is able to settle the mind on the gate of the path, then, as the path grows exalted, Māra grows correspondingly active — hence one must properly recognize demonic affairs. Here, this is explained in three parts: distinguishing the different kinds of demonic dharma; clarifying the marks of demonic affairs arising; and clarifying the methods for defeating demons.

zh:
第一、分別魔法不同，魔有四種：一者、煩惱魔；二者、陰入界魔；三者、死魔；四者、欲界天子魔。一、煩惱魔者，即是三毒、九十八使、取、有、流、扼、縛、蓋、纏、惱、結等，皆能破壞修道之事，如《摩訶衍論》偈說：
欲是汝初軍，憂愁為第二，
饑渴為第三，觸愛為第四，
睡眠第五軍，怖畏為第六，
疑悔為第七，瞋恚為第八，
利養虛稱九，自高蔑人十。
如是等軍眾，厭沒出家人。
我以禪智力，破汝此諸軍，
得成佛道已，度脫一切人。
en: First, distinguishing the different kinds of demonic dharma: there are four kinds of demon — the demon of affliction; the demon of the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements; the demon of death; and the demon of the desire realm's Heavenly Son.

First, the demon of affliction: this is precisely the three poisons, the ninety-eight latent tendencies, grasping, existence, the outflows, the yokes, the bonds, the hindrances, the entanglements, the vexations, the fetters, and the rest — all able to destroy the work of cultivating the path. As the Mahāyāna treatise says in verse:
"Desire is your first army, sorrow the second;
Hunger and thirst the third, contact and craving the fourth;
Sleep the fifth army, fear the sixth;
Doubt and regret the seventh, anger the eighth;
Profit and empty fame the ninth, self-exaltation and contempt for others the tenth.
Such armies as these overwhelm and submerge the one gone forth.
Through the power of dhyāna and wisdom, I shall break through these very armies of yours,
And, having accomplished the buddha-path, shall liberate every person."

zh: 二、陰界入魔，為五陰、十二入、十八界，一切名色繫縛眾生，陰覆行者清淨善根，功德智慧不得增長，故名為魔。所謂欲界陰入，乃至色、無色界陰入亦如是。行者若心不了受著，悉名為魔。若能不受不著，觀如虛空，不為覆障，即破魔業。三、死魔者，一切生死業報，輪轉不息，皆名為魔。復次，若行人欲發心修道，便得病命終，或為他害，不得修道，即為廢。今修習聖道，比至後世，因緣轉異，忘失本心，皆名魔事。復次，行者當修道時，慮死不活，便愛著其身而不修道，亦是死魔所攝。四、天子魔者，即是波旬。此魔是佛法怨讐，常恐行人出離其界，故令諸鬼神眷屬作種種惱亂，破壞行者善根，是為他化自在天子魔。
en: Second, the demon of the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements: the five aggregates, the twelve sense-bases, and the eighteen elements — every name and form binding sentient beings — obscure the practitioner's own pure wholesome roots, so that merit and wisdom fail to grow; hence they are named demons. This holds for the aggregates and sense-bases of the desire realm, and likewise for those of the form and formless realms as well. If the practitioner's mind fails to understand this and remains attached, all of it is named demonic; but if one is able to remain free of both reception and attachment, contemplating it as though empty space, it no longer serves as any obscuring obstruction, and the demon's own work is thereby broken through.

Third, the demon of death: every karmic result of birth-and-death, turning on without cease, is named demonic. Furthermore: if a practitioner, wishing to give rise to the resolve to cultivate the path, instead falls ill and dies, or is harmed by another, and so fails to cultivate the path — this, too, is an abandonment of practice. Even should one continue cultivating the noble path into a subsequent life, causes and conditions having shifted and changed, one's original resolve forgotten — all of this, too, is named demonic affairs. Furthermore: if the practitioner, at the time of cultivating the path, worries that death will come and that one will not survive, and so becomes attached to their own body instead of cultivating the path, this too is subsumed under the demon of death.

Fourth, the demon of the Heavenly Son: this is precisely Pāpīyas. This demon is the sworn enemy of the Buddhadharma, constantly fearing that the practitioner might escape from its own domain — hence it sends its various spirit-retinues to cause every kind of disturbance, destroying the practitioner's wholesome roots. This is the demon of the Heavenly Son of the Heaven of Free Enjoyment of Others' Emanations.

The four classical demons scale outward from the most intimate to the most cosmic: affliction (one's own mental defilements), the aggregates (the very constituents of body and mind), death (the basic condition of embodied existence), and finally an actual external adversary, Pāpīyas — the same "killer" etymology already introduced in fascicle 3's note on distinguishing genuine wholesome marks from demonic ones. The Mahāyāna treatise's ten-army verse (desire, sorrow, hunger, craving, sleep, fear, doubt, anger, vanity, contempt) doubles as a fairly complete inventory of what actually derails a meditation practice, framed as literal combatants a practitioner must defeat rather than as abstract categories.

items.en: The Marks of the Four Demons Arising

zh: 第二、明四魔發相者：若煩惱魔，如前不善根性中三毒等分煩惱中廣說。若陰入界魔發相，如前不善及善根性中發種種色心境界說；若死魔發相，如前病患法中廣說。所以者何？病為死因。若鬼神魔者，今當分別說。鬼神魔有三種：一者、精媚；二者、垖惕鬼；三者、魔羅。
en: Second, clarifying the marks of the four demons arising: as for the demon of affliction, this is explained at length above, within the three poisons and the equal-portion affliction, in the discussion of unwholesome capacity. As for the marks of the demon of the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements arising, this is explained above, within the various states of form and mind arising, in the discussion of both unwholesome and wholesome capacity. As for the marks of the demon of death arising, this is explained at length above, within the dharma of illness — why is this? Because illness is the very cause of death.
As for the demon of spirits, this shall now be distinguished. Spirit-demons are of three kinds: spirit-glamours; mischievous spirits; and Māra proper.

zh: 精媚者，十二時獸變化，作種種形色，或作少男、少女、老宿之形，及可畏身相等非一，以惱行人。各當其時而來，善須別識。若多卯時來者，必是狐、兔、狢等，說其名字，精媚即散。餘十一時形相，類此可知。二、垖惕鬼者，亦作種種惱亂行人，或如蟲緣人頭面鑽刺熠熠，或擊攊人兩掖下，或乍抱持於人，或復言說音聲喧鬧，及作諸獸之形，異相非一，來惱行人者，應即覺知，一心閉眼，陰而罵之，作是言：「我今識汝。汝是此閻浮提中食火嗅香偷臘吉支，邪見、喜破戒種。我今持戒，終不畏汝。」若出家人，應誦戒序，若在家人，應誦三歸、五戒、菩薩十重四十八輕戒等，鬼便却行，匍匐而去。如是作種種留難相貌，及除却之法，並如禪經中廣說。
en: As for spirit-glamours: these are the twelve double-hour animals in transformed shape, taking on various forms and colors — perhaps the form of a young man, a young woman, or an elder, and other such fearsome bodily forms not of one kind only — in order to trouble the practitioner. Each comes at its own proper hour, and one must properly learn to distinguish them. If one comes for the most part during the hour of the rabbit, it must be a fox-spirit, a hare-spirit, a badger-spirit, or the like — speaking its name aloud causes the spirit-glamour to disperse at once. The forms belonging to the remaining eleven double-hours may be understood by this same pattern.

Second, as for mischievous spirits: these, too, cause every kind of disturbance to the practitioner — crawling like insects over a person's head and face, pricking and tingling; striking or tickling under both armpits; suddenly embracing a person; or making loud, clamorous sounds and speech, and taking on the forms of various beasts, in strange forms not of one kind only. Should such a spirit come to trouble the practitioner, one should recognize it at once, closing the eyes with a single-pointed mind, and silently rebuke it, saying: "I now recognize you. You are, within this Jambudvīpa, a fire-eating, fragrance-sniffing toulajizhi (偷臘吉支), a seed of wrong view delighting in breaking the precepts. I now uphold the precepts, and shall never fear you." If one is ordained, one should recite the preamble to the precepts; if a layperson, one should recite the three refuges, the five precepts, or the bodhisattva's ten grave and forty-eight lesser precepts — and the spirit will then retreat, crawling away. Such various forms of hindrance as these, and the methods for dispelling them, are explained at length in the Chan Sūtra.

zh: 三、魔羅惱亂者，是魔多作三種相來破行人：一、作違情事，即是作可畏五塵；二、作順情事，即是作可愛五塵令人心著；三、作非違非順事，即是作平品五塵動亂行者。是故魔名殺者，復名華箭，亦並名五箭，射五情故。一情中有三種境，對情而惱行者，五情合有十五種境。
en: Third, as for the disturbance caused by Māra proper: this demon, for the most part, creates three kinds of appearance in order to destroy the practitioner. First, creating matters contrary to one's feelings — that is, creating fearsome objects among the five sense-objects. Second, creating matters in accord with one's feelings — that is, creating lovely objects among the five sense-objects, causing the mind to become attached. Third, creating matters neither contrary nor in accord — that is, creating neutral objects among the five sense-objects that nonetheless disturb the practitioner. Hence Māra is named "the killer," and is also called "the flower-arrow," and, further still, "the five arrows," since it shoots the five faculties of feeling. Within each single faculty there are three kinds of object, each troubling the practitioner in relation to that faculty — the five faculties together thus having fifteen kinds of object in all.

zh: 色中三者：一、順情色，或作父母、兄弟、諸佛形像、端正男女可愛之境，令人心著；二、色中違者，或作虎、狼、師子、羅剎之形，種種可畏像來怖行者；三、色中非違非順者，但作平品之形色，亦不令人生愛，亦不令人生怖，皆能動亂人心，令失禪定，故名為魔。餘諸情中，亦當如是分別，但約塵相有異。行者若不別諸邪偽，則為所壞，狂亂作罪，裸形無恥，起種種過，破他善事，毀損三寶，非可具說，或時得病致死，必須慎之，善加覺識。
en: Among the three within form: first, form in accord with one's feelings — perhaps taking the form of one's parents, siblings, or the images of various buddhas, or a lovely object of a handsome man or woman, causing the mind to become attached. Second, form contrary to one's feelings — perhaps taking the form of a tiger, a wolf, a lion, or a rākṣasa, various fearsome images coming to frighten the practitioner. Third, form neither contrary nor in accord — simply taking on neutral forms and colors, causing neither love nor fear to arise, yet still able to disturb the mind, causing the loss of dhyāna-concentration; hence it, too, is named demonic. The same distinctions should be understood to hold for every other faculty as well, differing only in terms of the particular sense-object involved. Should the practitioner fail to distinguish these various deviant illusions, one will be undone by them — thrown into deranged conduct and wrongdoing, going about naked and shameless, giving rise to every kind of fault, destroying others' wholesome undertakings, and damaging the Triple Gem — matters not possible to describe in full; at times, one may even fall ill and die from it. One must therefore be exceedingly cautious, applying careful recognition.

zh: 問曰：何故不約法塵對意根中論三種魔事？答曰：從多為論，一切魔事多從五情中入，故但說五情，細而論檢，意根中亦不無三種惱亂之事，類而可知。復次，諸大乘經中辨種種六塵中幻偽，對意根魔事起相，是中廣說，故《大品經》云：「如是等魔事魔罪不說不教，當知即是菩薩惡知識。」
en: Question: why are the three kinds of demonic affairs not discussed in terms of the dharma-object paired with the mind-faculty? Answer: speaking in terms of what is most common, demonic affairs, for the most part, enter through the five faculties of feeling — hence only these five faculties are discussed here. Examined closely, however, the mind-faculty, too, is certainly not without its own three kinds of disturbance; this may be understood by the same pattern. Furthermore, the various Mahāyāna sūtras discuss, at length, the illusory falseness within the various six sense-objects, and the marks of demonic affairs arising in relation to the mind-faculty specifically — hence the Larger Sūtra says: "Such demonic affairs and demonic offenses as these, if not spoken of and not taught, should be known as the bodhisattva's evil companion."

The three-kind scheme applied to each of the five faculties (pleasant, frightening, neutral — fifteen states in all) is structurally identical to the fifteen wholesome marks and fifteen unwholesome marks already given earlier in this fascicle, but reorganized around a different axis: not what kind of affliction is present, but what emotional pull an object exerts, regardless of content. The insistence that even a neutral, unremarkable state "disturbs the mind" and therefore counts as demonic is the section's least intuitive but most practically important claim — demonic interference isn't defined by its content being frightening or alluring, but simply by whatever succeeds in breaking concentration.

quiz.q: Which set belongs to the ten conditions for treating illness with the mind?
options: faith, application, diligence, dwelling in the object, distinguishing the cause
quiz.why: "The ten conditions are: faith; application; diligence; constantly dwelling within the object; distinguishing the illness's cause; skillful means; sustained practice over time; knowing what to take up and what to set aside; skillfully guarding and protecting oneself; and recognizing obstruction."

quiz.q: For "diligence" among the ten conditions, what is taken as the measure?
options: applying it single-mindedly without pause, taking sweat as the measure
quiz.why: "What is meant by diligence? Applying it with single-minded devotion, without pause, taking the appearance of sweat as the measure of its effect."

options: not speaking of one's benefit to others, and not doubting or denouncing the method before any harm occurs
quiz.why: "What is meant by recognizing obstruction? Not speaking of one's benefit to others, and not doubting or denouncing the method before any harm has actually occurred. If one relies on these ten conditions in treatment, there is certain to be an effect."

quiz.q: What are "sustained practice" and "knowing what to take up and set aside"?
options: sustained: keep practicing without counting days even if no immediate benefit; knowing: use diligently where it helps, set aside where it harms
quiz.why: "What is meant by sustained practice over time? Even if the method brings no immediate benefit, continuing to practice it without ever abandoning it, regardless of how many days or months pass. What is meant by knowing what to take up and what to set aside? Knowing that where it benefits, one should apply it diligently, and where it causes harm, one should set it aside."

quiz.q: How does the text explain Māra, and why must demonic affairs be recognized?
options: Māra means "the killer," seizing the wealth of merit and killing the life of wisdom; as the path grows exalted, Māra grows active
quiz.why: "Māra, in the Qin-dynasty translation, means 'the killer.' It seizes the wealth of the practitioner's merit and kills the very life of wisdom ... If one is able to settle the mind on the gate of the path, then, as the path grows exalted, Māra grows correspondingly active."

quiz.q: What are the four kinds of demon?
options: affliction, aggregates-sense-bases-elements, death, the desire realm's Heavenly Son
quiz.why: "There are four kinds of demon — the demon of affliction; the demon of the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements; the demon of death; and the demon of the desire realm's Heavenly Son." Spirit-glamours and the rest are kinds of spirit-demon.

quiz.q: In the verse on Māra's armies, what are the first and the tenth?
options: desire is the first; self-exaltation and contempt for others the tenth
quiz.why: "Desire is your first army, sorrow the second; / Hunger and thirst the third, contact and craving the fourth; / Sleep the fifth army, fear the sixth; / Doubt and regret the seventh, anger the eighth; / Profit and empty fame the ninth, self-exaltation and contempt for others the tenth."

quiz.q: A practitioner who worries over death, clings to the body, and does not cultivate falls under which demon?
quiz.why: "If the practitioner, at the time of cultivating the path, worries over death and clings to life, and so becomes attached to their own body instead of cultivating the path, this too is subsumed under the demon of death."

quiz.q: What are spirit-glamours, and how are they dealt with?
options: the twelve double-hour animals in transformed shape, each at its hour; one coming at the hour of the rabbit is a fox, hare, or badger — naming it disperses it
quiz.why: "Spirit-glamours: these are the twelve double-hour animals in transformed shape ... Each comes at its own proper hour ... If one comes for the most part during the hour of the rabbit, it must be a fox-spirit, a hare-spirit, a badger-spirit, or the like — speaking its name aloud causes the spirit-glamour to disperse at once."

quiz.q: Māra proper mostly creates which three kinds of appearance to destroy the practitioner?
options: contrary to feeling (fearsome objects), in accord (lovely objects), neither (neutral objects)
quiz.why: "First, creating matters contrary to one's feelings — that is, creating fearsome objects among the five sense-objects. Second, creating matters in accord with one's feelings — that is, creating lovely objects ... Third, creating matters neither contrary nor in accord — that is, creating neutral objects." Five faculties times three give fifteen.
